jobs.title: Legal Solutions Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Legal Solutions Engineer

Edinburgh
London

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents, and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling, and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe, and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The Role

Legal Solutions Engineers turn the product into real outcomes for customers.

You’ll work with customers after purchase to design, configure, and implement legal workflows inside Wordsmith. This role sits close to the customer, helping them embed the platform into how their legal function actually operates.

It’s part implementation, part problem solving, and part advisory. You’ll combine legal understanding with product knowledge to help customers get meaningful value from the platform.

What you’ll do

Customer Implementation

  • Lead implementation projects for new customers

  • Design workflows and automation tailored to each organisation

  • Configure the platform to support real legal use cases

Solution Design

  • Work directly with legal teams and Legal Ops leaders to understand how they operate

  • Translate legal processes into structured workflows and AI-enabled automation

  • Advise on best practices for implementing legal technology

Customer Success & Expansion

  • Support onboarding and early adoption

  • Help customers expand into additional workflows and use cases

  • Partner with Account Management to identify growth opportunities

Product Feedback

  • Surface patterns, insights, and recurring requests to Product and Engineering

  • Help shape how the product evolves based on real usage

What we’re looking for

  • Experience in legal tech, legal operations, or process transformation

  • Strong understanding of how in-house legal teams work

  • Ability to manage customer projects and guide stakeholders through change

  • Comfortable working across legal and technical domains

  • Structured thinker — you can turn messy processes into clear systems

  • Strong communication skills and confidence working directly with customers

Typical backgrounds include:

  • Legal Engineers

  • Legal Operations professionals

  • Lawyers who have moved into legal tech

  • Implementation or solutions consultants in SaaS with a legal background

How we work

We’re an in-office team in Edinburgh. We work together because it helps us collaborate closely across product, engineering, and customer teams. You should expect to be in the office as your default.

This is a high ownership role. You’ll be trusted to run projects, work directly with customers, and drive outcomes without heavy oversight.

The problems are often not fully defined. Part of the role is bringing structure and clarity to how legal work gets done.

Why this role matters

The value of legal technology comes from how it’s implemented.

Legal Solutions Engineers ensure customers successfully embed Wordsmith into their workflows and see real impact.

This role sits at the centre of that.

What you can expect

  • Direct impact on customer outcomes and product adoption

  • Close collaboration with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams

  • A chance to shape how legal teams use AI in practice

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

Product Engineer

Edinburgh/London

Wordsmith

Why this role is different

Our engineering team is not using AI as a feature. It’s how we build.

Engineers here are expected to explore, test, and apply AI directly in how we design and ship product. There’s no heavy process, no layers of approval, and no hesitation around new approaches.

If something works, we use it. If it doesn’t, we move on quickly.

You’ll have the freedom to experiment, shape how AI is used in the product, and push beyond the patterns most teams are still stuck in.

The Role

You’ll build product features end to end, working across frontend and backend, and ship AI-native workflows used by real customers.

You’ll work closely with design, product, and legal engineers to turn complex problems into simple, high-quality user experiences.

This is a role for someone who wants to move fast, stay close to users, and have a real impact on what gets built.

What you’ll do

  • Own features end to end across frontend and backend

  • Build AI-native workflows using LLMs and structured data

  • Collaborate closely with design, product, and legal engineering

  • Ship quickly, learn from users, and iterate

  • Contribute to architecture, tooling, and engineering practices

  • Help define how we use AI across the product

What we’re looking for

  • 4+ years building high-quality web products

  • Strong experience with modern frontend tools (React, Next.js, TypeScript)

  • Backend experience (Python, Node, AWS or similar)

  • Strong product instincts — you care about UX, clarity, and outcomes

  • Comfortable working in fast-moving environments with evolving systems

  • Interest in AI and how it changes how software is built

Bonus:

  • Experience with LLMs, prompt design, or AI workflows

  • Background in building internal tools or complex workflows

How we work

We’re an in-office team in Edinburgh/London. We work together because it helps us build faster, collaborate closely, and make better product decisions. You should expect to be in the office as your default.

This is a high trust environment. Engineers have real ownership over what they build and how they build it.

We keep process light and focus on shipping, learning, and improving quickly.

What you can expect

  • Real ownership over product and technical decisions

  • The chance to work at the frontier of AI-native product development

  • A team of engineers, designers, and domain experts working closely together

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

Why Wordsmith

We’re growing quickly, shipping fast, and solving real problems for customers.

The product is evolving rapidly, and engineering plays a central role in how far and how fast we can go.

If you want to build with AI as a core part of your workflow, not just a layer on top, this is a strong place to do it.

Sales Development Representative

Edinburgh

 

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

The Role

We’re hiring a Sales Development Representative (SDR) to spearhead our outbound engine and book high-quality opportunities with in-house legal teams.

This is the frontline of our growth. You’ll be responsible for finding the right accounts, crafting compelling outreach, and breaking into companies. You’ll work hand-in-hand with our Account Executives (AEs) and Marketing teams to build a predictable pipeline.

This is an early-stage environment. Things move fast, priorities shift, and there isn’t always a clear playbook. You’ll need to be resilient, highly organized, and willing to experiment with new ways to get a prospect’s attention.

What you’ll do

  • Build and execute targeted outbound campaigns (email, cold calling, LinkedIn) to general counsel and legal leaders.

  • Consistently hit and exceed monthly meeting-booked and pipeline targets.

  • Partner closely with AEs to strategize on key accounts and ensure smooth handoffs.

  • Act as a feedback loop for Marketing and Product by tracking what messaging resonates most with the market.

  • Maintain meticulous CRM data — keeping track of accounts, prospects, and outreach activity.

What we’re looking for

  • SaaS sales or lead generation experience (experience selling to legal, finance, or compliance is a major plus, but not required).

  • A relentless work ethic — you aren't afraid of the phone and view "no" as data, not a deterrent.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can cut through the noise with clear, value-led messaging.

  • High curiosity and coachability; you want to master the product, the market, and the art of sales.

  • High ownership — you take responsibility for outcomes, not just logging activities.

  • Organized, consistent, and reliable with excellent time management.

How we work

We’re an in-office team. We work together because it makes us faster, sharper, and more effective. You should expect to be in the office our out visiting clients as your default.

This is a high performance environment. We set a high bar, move quickly, and expect people to take ownership of real problems.

There isn’t always a clear path. The people who do well here figure things out, stay close to the work, and keep pushing until they get to the right outcome.

This role requires patience, structure, and strong judgement. You’ll be trusted to run complex deals with a high degree of autonomy.

 

Why Wordsmith

We’re in a period of strong momentum — growing quickly, winning new customers, and expanding into larger accounts.

The product is landing well, the market is ready, and the team is scaling to meet demand.

If you want to be in the room, close meaningful deals, and grow quickly in a high bar environment, this is one of the best places to do it.

jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Product Designer

Edinburgh

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents, and disconnected systems.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling, and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe, and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The role

We're looking for someone who lives at the intersection of design and code. You'll work directly with product and engineering to frame the problem, design the flows, then prototype, build, and polish the experiences that make Wordsmith feel effortless, even when the workflows underneath are anything but. This role suits someone who thinks like a designer and builds like an engineer, or the other way round.

You'll design products where the behaviour is not always fixed, the inputs are messy, and the outcome still has to feel simple and reliable. You'll own that outcome end to end, and you'll be trusted to run with it on your own.

What you'll do

  • Design and build the UX and UI: the flows, components, and interactions that simplify complex legal workflows

  • Rapidly prototype new concepts in code to validate ideas before committing to a full build

  • Bridge design and engineering: turn designs into shipped code, and push design forward through technical craft

  • Own the quality of UI implementation across the product, from pixel-perfect execution to the small interactions that make it feel alive

  • Help define product direction, frame ambiguous problems, and design the end-to-end flows behind the interface

  • Contribute to the design system and component libraries that let the team ship faster

  • Use AI as part of how you work, to explore, prototype, and think past traditional UX and UI patterns

You might be a fit if

  • You can shape the direction of projects and bring people with you. You've earned the trust of engineers, PMs, and senior stakeholders before, and you know how to move a team without holding a mandate

  • You can build and ship your own front-end (TypeScript, React, CSS, animation). AI writes a lot of it now, so the real bar is taste and judgment: knowing what good looks like and getting it the last 10%

  • You're self-sufficient: you can take a problem from ambiguity to shipped experience on your own, no hand-holding required

  • You have an eye for detail and care deeply about craft, in the flows and logic as much as the pixels

  • You finish what you start: polished and shipped, not left at good enough

  • You move fast, prototyping ideas in hours, not days

  • You think in systems and build reusable, maintainable UI

  • You're excited about AI and want to help define new interaction paradigms for an entire industry

Nice to have

  • Experience building or scaling design systems

  • Experience building developer tools, technical products, or other complex software for expert users

  • Formal design training, or a track record that makes it irrelevant

  • A real interest in how legal work actually gets done

How we work

We're an in-office team in Edinburgh. We work together because it helps us collaborate closely, move faster, and make better product decisions. Expect the office as your default. Design sits tightly with product and engineering, so you'll be in the room for the decisions, not working in isolation.

What you can expect

  • Real ownership over product direction and design decisions

  • Complex, meaningful problems at the intersection of AI and real-world legal work

  • A small team of engineers, designers, and domain experts who ship

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

At Wordsmith, you'll build category-defining tools that change how an entire industry works. If you want your design work to have real-world impact at scale, we'd love to hear from you.

  • Act as the voice of the in-house customer within the GTM team, feeding commercial and product teams with insight on how corporate legal departments think, prioritise, and buy.

Market engagement

  • Help develop commercial messaging, content, and collateral that speaks directly to the priorities of GCs, Legal Ops leaders, and in-house teams.

Essential

  • Qualified attorney with experience in an in-house legal team — whether at a corporation, financial institution, or high-growth company. Direct experience of the operational pressures, budget constraints, and strategic priorities facing corporate legal is central to this role.

  • Strong understanding of how in-house legal departments are structured and how decisions get made — from the GC down to legal ops as well as interacting with other members of a company..

  • Ability to engage credibly across a range of in-house stakeholders: legal leadership, legal ops professionals, procurement, and business clients.

  • Executive presence and communication skills — comfortable presenting to a GC, facilitating a workshop with a legal ops team, or running a business case discussion with a CFO.

  • A genuine ability to translate across disciplines: bridging legal, commercial, technical, and operational conversations without losing the thread.

  • Curiosity about AI and a genuine conviction that it will reshape the in-house legal function.

Valued

  • Experience in legal operations, legal tech procurement, or technology implementation within a legal department.

  • Familiarity with the tools and systems common in in-house environments (contract lifecycle management, matter management, e-billing, compliance platforms).

  • Exposure to change management or large-scale technology rollout programmes.

  • Prior experience in a client-facing or commercial role, including secondment or business development.

  • Comfort operating in fast-moving, high-ambiguity environments with a founder and builder mentality.

Why this role matters

You will be the person helping some of the world's most sophisticated legal departments navigate a genuinely transformative shift in how they operate.

Your work will directly influence product direction, GTM strategy, and how the company builds its in-house market globally.

You will have the autonomy to shape how this function evolves — this is a high-ownership role at a company moving fast.

You will work with a sharp, motivated team that operates with intensity and takes genuine ownership of outcomes.

What you can expect

The opportunity to be at the forefront engaging with how inhouse lawyers and businesses are thinking about AI.

The chance to collaborate with product, engineering and GTM in an environment where you can learn and contribute meaningfully.

How we work

We’re an in-office team in New York. We work together because it helps us collaborate closely across product, engineering, and GTM teams. You should expect to be in the office as your default.

This is a high ownership role. You’ll be trusted to run projects, work directly with customers, and drive outcomes without heavy oversight.

Wordsmith

The role

We’re hiring a Support Engineer to provide fast, thoughtful and technically rigorous help to Wordsmith customers.

You’ll own technical questions and incidents from first response through to resolution. You’ll understand what the customer is trying to achieve, reproduce reported behaviour, investigate the underlying cause and explain the outcome clearly.

This is more than scripted customer support. You’ll be expected to investigate application behaviour at a technical level, including reading logs and tracing issues through the product and its codebase. Where appropriate to your experience, you may also propose and submit code fixes through our normal engineering review and release process.

Wordsmith supports customers globally through a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the standard hours for your region and hand over unresolved issues clearly to colleagues in other regions. There is no routine expectation that you work another region’s hours.

What you’ll do

  • Own technical support requests — triage, investigate and resolve customer questions and incidents from first response to confirmed resolution.

  • Diagnose problems thoroughly — gather the right context, reproduce reported behaviour, inspect logs and data, and trace issues through the product and codebase.

  • Resolve technical issues — correct configuration or usage problems directly and collaborate with Engineering when a product or infrastructure change is required.

  • Contribute code fixes where appropriate — depending on your experience, propose and submit well-tested fixes through the standard engineering review and deployment process.

  • Communicate clearly — give customers timely and accurate updates, explain technical issues without unnecessary jargon and set honest expectations.

  • Manage escalations — bring in Engineering, Product or other specialists when needed while retaining ownership of the case and its communication.

  • Support global handovers — document investigation, impact, current status and next actions so colleagues in another region can continue work without losing momentum.

  • Protect service quality — recognise high-impact incidents quickly, follow the appropriate escalation process and contribute to incident reviews.

  • Build customer knowledge — create and maintain troubleshooting guides, known-issue documentation and help-centre content.

  • Reduce repeat problems — identify patterns in support demand and recommend improvements to the product, documentation, tooling and customer experience.

  • Improve support operations — help develop service levels, escalation paths, reporting and technical-support processes as the function scales.

The tools you'll use

  • Pylon is our helpdesk. Customer tickets, accounts, internal notes and escalations all live here.

  • GitHub. A little Git and GitHub knowledge is all you need.

  • Wordsmith itself. You'll use the product the way our customers do, which is how you'll reproduce what they report and learn how in-house legal teams work.

  • AI tools. You'll work with AI every day and be expected to check its output rather than trust it. Curiosity about how AI behaves, including when it's wrong, matters more than experience with any one tool.

  • The command line. Basic Bash is useful for moving around files, searching logs and running small scripts. Python or similar is a bonus. You don't need to be an expert; we'll help you build this up.

How we measure succes
We measure success on how quickly customers get a first response and on keeping customer satisfaction high. The people who do well here explain complex ideas simply, take ownership of an issue until it's confirmed resolved, stay calm under pressure, and document what they tested with care and precision.

A week in the role

  • Work your region's ticket queue in Pylon: triage, reproduce in Wordsmith, then resolve or escalate.

  • Investigate with logs, browser tools and the codebase to find the root cause.

  • Explain the outcome to the customer in plain language.

  • Write a clear handover note for the next region before you finish.

  • Flag patterns to Product, with the customer evidence behind them.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience in technical support, product support, software engineering, solutions engineering or another customer-facing technical role.

  • Strong diagnostic ability — you can work methodically from symptoms to root cause rather than relying on guesswork.

  • A working understanding of modern web applications, APIs, authentication, integrations and common browser or network issues.

  • Experience using diagnostic information such as application logs, monitoring tools, browser developer tools and database queries.

  • Enough familiarity with software code to navigate a codebase, follow application logic and use it to investigate reported behaviour.

  • Clear customer communication — you can remain calm under pressure, set expectations honestly and explain complex issues at the right level of detail.

  • Strong ownership — you remain responsible for moving an issue forward even when other teams need to contribute.

  • Sound prioritisation — you can assess urgency and customer impact and recognise when an issue requires immediate escalation.

  • Care and precision — you document what you tested, avoid unsupported conclusions and confirm that the customer’s problem has actually been resolved.

  • Interest in AI systems — you’re curious about how AI-enabled products behave and comfortable investigating issues that may not always be deterministic.

  • No legal background is required, but you should be motivated to learn how in-house legal teams work.

Desirable, but not essential

  • Experience writing and debugging production software.

  • The ability to create automated tests and submit code fixes for engineering review.

  • Experience supporting AI-enabled or data-intensive applications.

  • Familiarity with incident-management and observability tools.

How we work

We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh. You should expect to work from the office as your default.

We support customers globally using a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the normal hours agreed for your region and create clear handovers when an issue needs to continue beyond them. Any exceptional on-call or out-of-hours arrangements would be agreed and communicated separately.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. Support is a core part of the product experience, and we expect it to be technically credible, responsive and human.

You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Transformation and Customer Success. Customer Success owns adoption and customer health; Transformation owns implementation; Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth; and Support Engineering owns technical investigation and resolution.

Why Wordsmith

You’ll support a fast-growing product used for important work inside some of the world’s most ambitious organisations.

Because we’re building in a new technical category, the problems are interesting. You’ll work across software behaviour, integrations, data and AI systems rather than following a script.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape our support tooling and operating model, influence the product through direct customer evidence, and develop towards senior support engineering, support leadership, solutions engineering or product engineering.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Wordsmith
Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we're growing fast.

In-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems. Wordsmith brings that work into one place: requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We're built for in-house legal, not law firms. More than 500 companies use Wordsmith, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage. We're backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others.

The role

We're hiring an Enablement Lead to own how customers learn Wordsmith, and how they become confident, self-sufficient users of it.

You'll own onboarding, training and enablement end to end: Legal AI fundamentals, product and feature overviews, self-paced certifications, and re-enablement for customers who've stalled. You'll teach both ends of the customer organisation: the lawyers and business users in Wordsmith every day, and the champions and admins who support their colleagues.

This is an enablement role, not a delivery or commercial one. You won't own implementation, technical support, renewals, account growth or a sales quota. Your focus is capability: do customers know how to use Wordsmith well, and can they keep learning without us?

What you'll do

  • Own customer onboarding. Design and run the journey that takes a newly implemented customer to a confident, capable team, and keep improving it.

  • Teach Legal AI fundamentals. Build the curriculum that helps legal teams understand what AI agents do well, where judgement stays with them, and how to work alongside the technology.

  • Run live training. Lead onboarding sessions, product walkthroughs and feature deep dives for lawyers, business users and admins of every technical confidence level.

  • Build the self-paced academy. Create online certifications and learning paths so customers can train new joiners and refresh skills on their own.

  • Maintain the enablement library. Keep guides and product overviews accurate as Wordsmith ships, and retire what's out of date.

  • Re-enable struggling customers. Diagnose why adoption has stalled and run focused programmes that get teams back to self-sufficiency.

  • Train the champions. Equip customer champions and admins to teach their own colleagues, so capability compounds inside each account.

  • Shape in-app help. Work with Product to build guidance, walkthroughs and prompts into Wordsmith itself.

  • Measure whether learning worked. Define what a trained, self-sufficient customer looks like, track it, and use the evidence to change what we teach.

  • Partner across customer teams. Work with Transformation, Customer Success, Support Engineering and Product so enablement reflects real implementations, questions and product changes.

What we're looking for

  • 3–5 years in customer enablement, training, onboarding, customer education, implementation or a similar customer-facing role where teaching was central.

  • You design learning, not just deliver it. You can turn a complex product into a curriculum with a clear sequence and outcomes.

  • Confidence in front of a room, in person and on video, with senior lawyers as readily as with day-to-day users.

  • Experience building self-paced content (courses, certifications, guides, video) and a view on what makes people finish it.

  • A clear, warm communication style that makes unfamiliar ideas easy to grasp without oversimplifying them.

  • Strong organisation: you can run several programmes, sessions and content deadlines at once without losing detail.

  • Comfort with data. You can read product-usage information, spot where learning hasn't landed and act on it.

  • Curiosity about AI and legal technology. You don't need a legal background, but you'll want to learn the product and our customers' work deeply.

  • A strong learning mindset: you welcome feedback, apply coaching and want to grow quickly.

How we work

We're an in-person team in Edinburgh, so expect to work from the office or visit customers by default. We set a high bar, move quickly and give people real ownership. There won't always be a playbook, so you'll bring curiosity, structure and persistence.

You'll work closely with the VP of Transformation and with Customer Success, Account Management and Product. Each customer team has a clear remit:

  • Transformation leads implementation

  • Support Engineering resolves technical issues

  • Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth

  • Customer Success owns adoption, customer health and value realisation

  • Enablement owns onboarding, training and customer capability

Why join Wordsmith

Wordsmith is growing quickly, winning new customers and expanding inside larger organisations. Because Legal AI is new to almost everyone who buys it, teaching it well is one of the highest-leverage things we can do.

You'll join early enough to define what customer enablement at Wordsmith is: the curriculum, the certifications, and the standard for what a confident user looks like. You'll work directly with ambitious legal teams, learn the product deeply and develop fast in a high-performing team.

  • You care about security and doing things properly, not just quickly

  • You're happy working on-site in Edinburgh and hands-on with real hardware

  • Exposure to identity and device tooling such as Okta, Google Workspace or Jamf

  • Experience with SOC 2 or security compliance

  • Having run or automated onboarding, endpoints or internal tools before

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the AI platform for in-house legal teams. Our customers use Wordsmith to move faster, automate the repetitive parts of legal work, and give their whole business quicker access to legal support. We're growing quickly, and every new customer we win deserves a brilliant experience from day one — that's where you come in.

About the role

We’re hiring a Customer Success Manager to help customers achieve lasting value from Wordsmith and own their renewal.

Once a customer has been implemented by our Transformation team, you’ll become their day-to-day success partner. You’ll help them embed Wordsmith into their organisation, increase meaningful adoption and demonstrate the impact the platform is having on their work.

You’ll own the customer journey from post-implementation handover through to renewal, connecting customer outcomes with retention. That means understanding what success looks like, building strong relationships, identifying risk early and managing the renewal process from initial planning through commercial conversations to signature.

You won’t own technical support or implementation. You will be accountable for adoption, customer health, value realisation and renewals across your portfolio, working with Account Management on expansion opportunities.

It’s an early-career role with meaningful responsibility and close support from our Head of Customer Success. You’ll receive coaching on managing customer relationships, leading renewal conversations and developing the commercial judgement to become an excellent CSM.

What you'll do

  • Own customer success plans — understand what each customer wants to achieve, agree measurable outcomes and keep progress visible.

  • Take customers forward after implementation — partner with our Transformation team to ensure a clear handover and help customers move from initial deployment to sustained adoption.

  • Drive adoption — use product data and customer conversations to identify gaps, activate dormant users and introduce relevant capabilities and use cases.

  • Build trusted relationships — develop strong connections with day-to-day users, internal champions, senior stakeholders and renewal decision-makers.

  • Lead customer conversations — run regular check-ins, adoption reviews and value reviews that connect product usage to meaningful business outcomes.

  • Monitor customer health — combine usage data, feedback and relationship insight to recognise disengagement or risk early.

  • Turn risk into action — build recovery plans and coordinate the right colleagues from Support, Transformation, Product or Account Management to address issues that could affect retention.

  • Own renewals from start to finish — maintain a clear renewal plan for every account, confirm decision-makers and procurement requirements, demonstrate value, lead commercial discussions within agreed parameters and coordinate proposals, contracts and signatures. You’ll have support from the Head of Customer Success on complex negotiations.

  • Keep renewal forecasts accurate — maintain a clear view of renewal dates, customer intent, risks and next steps, escalating early when a renewal needs additional support.

  • Partner with Account Management on growth — identify expansion opportunities and share the customer context and evidence of value needed to pursue them. Account Management owns expansion; you own the renewal.

  • Represent the customer — turn customer feedback into clear, useful insight for our Product, Support and Commercial teams.

  • Improve how we work — contribute to the playbooks, materials, processes and health measures that allow Customer Success and renewals to scale.

What we're looking for

  • Some experience in customer success, account management, consulting or another customer-facing environment. Recent graduates with strong relevant experience are also welcome.

  • A proactive approach - you don’t wait to be told what to do and are comfortable following up, asking questions and keeping work moving.

  • Strong relationship-building skills - you can listen carefully, establish trust and adapt to different personalities and levels of seniority.

  • Commercial awareness - you understand how adoption and demonstrated value contribute to retention and growth, and you’re comfortable developing the skills to discuss pricing, handle objections and secure renewals.

  • A clear, warm communication style - you can lead a conversation, write a concise follow-up and make unfamiliar ideas easy to understand.

  • Strong organisation - you can manage several customer relationships, renewal timelines and follow-up actions without losing attention to detail.

  • Confidence working with data - you can interpret product-usage and account-health information and turn it into practical action.

  • Curiosity about AI and legal technology - you don’t need a legal background, but you’ll want to learn the product and our customers’ work deeply.

  • A strong learning mindset - you welcome feedback, apply coaching and want to develop quickly. Previous experience owning renewals is helpful, but not essential.

Why Wordsmith

  • Ground-floor seat at a fast-growing AI company, with a front-row view of how modern legal teams adopt AI.

  • A role where you learn the full customer lifecycle — onboarding, support, adoption, renewal — the foundation for a career in customer success or commercial roles.

  • Direct access to customers and to the founding team; your feedback shapes the product.

  • A team that ships fast, cares about customers, and will invest in your growth.

How we work


We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh. You should expect to work from the office or visit customers as your default.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. There will not always be an established playbook, so you’ll need to bring curiosity, structure and persistence to unfamiliar situations.

You’ll receive regular support and coaching from the Head of Customer Success while progressively taking greater ownership of your customer relationships.

Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support Engineering resolves technical issues, Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth, and Customer Success owns adoption, customer health

The role

Legal Engineers turn the product into real outcomes for customers.

You’ll work with customers after purchase to design, configure, and implement legal workflows inside Wordsmith. This role sits close to the customer, helping them embed the platform into how their legal function actually operates.

It’s part implementation, part problem solving, and part advisory. You’ll combine legal understanding with product knowledge to help customers get meaningful value from the platform.

This is a technical, hands-on role. You don’t need to be a lawyer, and we’re not necessarily looking for one. We’re looking for analytical thinkers who are comfortable with technology and ideally have deployed legal tech before — people who can understand how a legal team works, then build the system that supports it. Where the work turns on legal judgement, we already have lawyers as part of the team who can bring the legal expertise.

What you’ll do

1. Customer Implementation

  • Lead implementation projects for new customers

  • Design workflows and automation tailored to each organisation

  • Configure the platform to support real legal use cases

  • Scope implementations for complex enterprise customers — use cases, sequencing, and where value will land first

2. Solution Design

  • Work directly with legal teams and Legal Ops leaders to understand how they operate

  • Translate legal processes into structured workflows and AI-enabled automation

  • Advise on best practices for implementing legal technology

  • Build and adapt playbooks with the customer, bringing in Legal Intelligence where clause language or negotiation positions need a lawyer’s judgement

3. Technical Build

  • Build integrations and connect Wordsmith to customers’ systems, knowing when to bring in Engineering

  • Build agents, skills, automations and workflows, from standard templates to complex multi-step processes

  • Take on complex reports and playbooks, leaving standard ones, such as a basic NDA blueprint, to the wider customer team

4. Escalation & Fixes

  • Reconfigure playbooks and workflows when a customer’s risk appetite or process changes

  • Act as the escalation point for technical issues and complex training questions from Support and Enablement

  • Run deeper health checks where a setup needs technical or process review

5. Customer Success & Expansion

  • Support onboarding and early adoption

  • Help customers expand into additional workflows and use cases

  • Create the template flows Enablement uses to demo and train on standard product workflows

  • Provide on-site embedded support where a customer needs hands-on technical help

6. Product Feedback

  • Surface patterns, insights, and recurring requests to Product and Engineering

  • Help shape how the product evolves based on real usage

What we’re looking for

  • Experience in legal tech, legal operations, or process transformation

  • Strong understanding of how in-house legal teams work

  • Ability to manage customer projects and guide stakeholders through change

  • Comfortable working across legal and technical domains

  • Technical enough to build integrations, agents and automations yourself, and to judge when a problem needs Engineering

  • A fixer’s instinct — comfortable diagnosing a live setup and reworking it when a customer’s needs change

  • Structured thinker — you can turn messy processes into clear systems

  • Strong communication skills and confidence working directly with customers

Typical backgrounds include

  • Prior Legal Engineering experience

  • Implementation or solutions consultants in SaaS (CLM / Legal Tech is a plus)

  • Legal Operations Professionals

How we work

We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh or London. You should expect to work from the office or visit customers as your default.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. There will not always be an established playbook, so you’ll need to bring curiosity, structure and persistence to unfamiliar situations.

You’ll sit in the Transformation team, reporting to the VP of Transformation, and work alongside Legal Intelligence, Enablement, Customer Success, Support Engineering and Product.

Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support Engineering resolves technical issues, Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth, Customer Success owns adoption, customer health and value realisation, and Enablement owns onboarding, training and customer capability.

Why Wordsmith

Wordsmith is growing quickly, winning new customers and expanding within larger organisations. How legal work gets rebuilt around AI is still being written, and Legal Engineers are the people writing it with our customers.

You’ll work directly with ambitious in-house legal teams, see how dozens of legal functions really operate, and take that back into a product you help shape. It is a rare place to combine legal judgement with building things.

  1. Own the Engagement

  • Run our most complex customer engagements end to end, from kickoff through go-live to handover

  • Build and own the project plan, including scope, milestones,dependencies, owners and timelines, and hold everyone to it

  • Be the customer's main point of contact for delivery, and the person accountable for getting them live

  1. Lead the Delivery Team

  • Coordinate Legal Engineers and Deployment Engineers so configuration and integration workstreams move in step

  • Sequence the work so dependencies are resolved before they block progress

  • Bring in Legal Intelligence, Support Engineering, Product and Engineering when the engagement needs them

  1. Stakeholders & Governance

  • Run kickoffs, steering committees and status reporting with General Counsel, Legal Ops, IT and procurement

  • Align stakeholders with competing priorities, and keep decisions, actions and changes documented

  • Manage scope carefully, agreeing changes explicitly rather than letting them drift

  1. Risk & Change

  • Identify delivery risk early, including resourcing, dependencies, customer readiness and timelines, and act on it

  • Escalate to the VP of Transformation with clear options when an engagement needs intervention

  • Help customers prepare their teams for change, working with Enablement on rollout and training

  1. Improve How We Deliver

  • Turn what you learn into delivery templates, governance models and planning standards for complex engagements

  • Share patterns and recurring blockers with the wider Transformation team and Product

What we're looking for

  • Experience running complex enterprise technology implementations or programmes, ideally SaaS and ideally legal tech

  • A track record of delivering multi-workstream projects on time, with many stakeholders and dependencies

  • Confident with senior stakeholders, including General Counsel, CIOs and procurement, and able to hold a room

  • Technical enough to understand integrations, SSO and configuration well enough to plan them and spot risk

  • Strong understanding of how in-house legal teams work, or the curiosity to learn it quickly

  • Disciplined about scope, governance and documentation without being bureaucratic

  • Calm under pressure, with the judgement to escalate at the right moment

  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication

Typical Backgrounds Include

  • Project or programme managers in enterprise SaaS

  • Delivery leads from technology consultancies

  • Legal Operations Professionals who have led a major technology rollout

  • Implementation managers in CLM or legal tech

Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support

Project Managers are the people who make those engagements succeed.

You'll work directly with ambitious in-house legal teams, see how dozens of legal functions really operate, and take that back into a product you help shape. You will lead experienced Legal Engineers and Deployment

You’ll own the operational backbone of our People function: payroll, global mobility, PEOs, commission and equity administration, HRIS, and the systems that keep everything in sync. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on clean operations, not a junior administrator position and not a People leadership seat.

You'll operate the frameworks our leadership and Finance set (pay philosophy, salary bands, commission structure, equity strategy). Your job is to implement those decisions accurately and on time, with a clear audit trail, and with the judgment to stop or escalate anything that doesn't fit the framework or lacks proper approval.

What You'll Do

  • Own payroll controls and monthly validation across UK payroll, PEOs, and other employment models, with clean reconciliation to Finance each month

  • Run visa and mobility operations end-to-end: sponsorships, relocations, compliance, right-to-work controls, and coordination with immigration advisers.

  • Manage commission review, approvals, exceptions, ns and payment accuracy each cycle; reconcile commission data between sales systems, Finance, and payroll

  • Own equity grant administration: approvals, documentation, vesting schedules, leaver events, exercises, cap table reconciliation and employee communications

  • Build and improve people workflows in Humans, Ashby and connected systems, using automation to remove manual steps from pay reviews, promotion packs, onboarding and routine queries.

  • Own onboarding, probation, employment changes, transfers, parental leave, and offboarding end-to-end: coordinate access, equipment, payroll and documentation across People, IT, Finance and hiring managers

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • 5+ years of People Operations or HR generalist experience in a scaling technology business or high-growth scaleup, with meaningful hands-on work in payroll, mobility, PEOs and benefits

  • Track record of building and running multi-country people processes from the ground up, not just maintaining existing structures.

  • Confidence owning payroll controls, global mobility operations and equity administration across multiple jurisdictions

  • Strong data literacy and experience with HRIS platforms, payroll systems and ATS integrations, with a bias toward automation over manual work

  • Clear written communicator who can produce clean documentation and audit-ready records

Valued

  • Experience independently owning multi-country payroll, mobility and equity through a scale up's growth phase.

  • Familiarity with PEO relationships, renewals and service management

  • Experience with commission administration and pooling

How We Work

We're an office-first team in London. You'll be based at our offices on Paul Street and expect to work in-office as your default. We work together because it helps us move faster, collaborate closely across Finance, IT and People, and stay sharp on detail.

This role sits at the center of trust for the whole company. We expect high standards of accuracy, timeliness and data integrity. You'll manage sensitive information and ensure payments, visas, and equity records are handled properly.

People will come to you with urgent requests and competing priorities. You need to stay organised, keep control of your workload, and know when to push back and when to escalate. This isn't a role for someone who needs a heavy process or lots of direction.

 
 

Why Wordsmith

We're scaling fast across product, commercial, and engineering, and People operations is foundational to that growth. Every new hire adds complexity to payroll, visas, benefits, and equity. Getting that right, automated, ed and audit-ready is what lets us move quickly without losing control.

This role is a key foundational hire. You'll be building the systems and processes that scale with us from ~130 people toward 300. You'll have real ownership over how the function works, and a clear seat in how we operate.

You'll report to our Head of People (or interim People leader, with a clear line to a future Head of People), work closely with Finance and leadership, and have meaningful say in how we run the function.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The role

Deployment Engineers own the technical side of getting Wordsmith live inside a customer.

Once a deal is signed, you’ll connect Wordsmith to the systems our customers already run on. That means identity and SSO, Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Google Workspace, Salesforce, document management, chat tools, and MCP connections to the wider AI and data stack. You’ll design how data and permissions flow between them, build and test the integrations, and work through each customer’s IT and security requirements until everything works in production.

It’s part integration engineering, part solutions architecture, and part customer-facing problem solving. You’ll be the technical lead on every deployment you own, the person customer IT teams talk to, and the person who works out how to make it work when an integration doesn’t behave as documented.

This is a technical, hands-on role. You don’t need to be a lawyer, and we’re not necessarily looking for one. We’re looking for engineers and technical consultants who understand identity, APIs and enterprise SaaS, and who enjoy making systems talk to each other. Your focus is the technical foundation the rest of the deployment runs on.

You’ll work side by side with our Legal Engineers on every deployment. While you connect Wordsmith to the customer’s systems, they configure the platform itself: workflows, agents, playbooks and automations built around how the legal team works. You’ll plan the deployment together, agree what each integration needs to support, and make sure the connections you build give their configuration the data, documents and permissions it depends on.

What you’ll do

1. Integrations

  • Own the integrations for each deployment, including SSO and SCIM, Microsoft 365, SharePoint and OneDrive, Google Workspace, Salesforce, document management and chat tools

  • Configure and connect Wordsmith to customers’ wider AI and data stack through MCP

  • Build, test and harden integrations so they hold up in production, not just in a demo

2. Identity, Security & Access

  • Set up identity and access, including SSO with Okta, Entra ID and Google, user provisioning, roles and permissions

  • Work through customers’ security reviews, IT questionnaires and data-handling requirements

  • Make sure permissions in Wordsmith respect the permissions in the systems it connects to

3. Technical Solution Design

  • Take the technical handover from Sales and confirm the customer’s systems landscape, constraints and integration scope

  • Design how data, documents and requests flow between Wordsmith and the customer’s tools

  • Advise customer IT on the right architecture for their environment and where the trade-offs sit

  • Work with Legal Engineers to agree what each integration needs to support the workflows, agents and playbooks they’re configuring

4. Technical Delivery & Escalation

  • Lead the technical workstream of each deployment, from environment setup and integration build through testing to go-live

  • Diagnose and fix integration issues, and act as the escalation point for technical problems during rollout

  • Know when a problem needs Engineering, and bring them a clear, reproducible case

5. Improve How We Integrate

  • Turn what you learn into reusable integration patterns, setup guides and technical runbooks

  • Feed connector gaps, API limitations and recurring requests back to Product and Engineering

What we’re looking for

  • Hands-on experience deploying and integrating enterprise SaaS in customer environments

  • Strong working knowledge of identity and access, including SSO (SAML, OIDC), SCIM provisioning, Okta, Entra ID or Google Workspace

  • Experience integrating with the Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Google Workspace or Salesforce ecosystems

  • Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, authentication flows and reading technical documentation. You can script or write code where it helps

  • Familiarity with MCP or other ways of connecting AI systems to tools and data, or a strong appetite to learn

  • Credible with customer IT and security teams. You can answer their questions and stand behind your architecture

  • Methodical troubleshooter who isolates problems, reproduces them and fixes them

  • Clear communicator who can explain a technical decision to a non-technical stakeholder

Typical backgrounds include

  • Deployment, integration or implementation engineers in SaaS

  • Solutions engineers or solutions architects

  • Technical consultants with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or Salesforce experience

  • IT or identity engineers who have moved into customer-facing roles

How we work

We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh or London. You should expect to work from the office or visit customers as your default.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. There will not always be an established playbook, so you’ll need to bring curiosity, structure and persistence to unfamiliar situations.

You’ll sit in the Transformation team, reporting to the VP of Transformation, and work closely with our Legal Engineers, alongside Legal Intelligence, Enablement, Customer Success, Support Engineering and Product.

Our customer teams have clear but closely connected responsibilities: Transformation leads implementation, Support Engineering resolves technical issues, Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth, Customer Success owns adoption, customer health and value realisation, and Enablement owns onboarding, training and customer capability.

Why Wordsmith

Wordsmith is growing quickly, winning new customers and expanding within larger organisations. Wordsmith is only as useful as the systems it connects to. Every new customer brings a different stack, and Deployment Engineers are the people who make Wordsmith work inside it.

You’ll work directly with ambitious in-house legal teams, see how dozens of legal functions really operate, and take that back into a product you help shape. You will work across enterprise identity, productivity and CRM platforms, and on MCP as it develops into a standard. You will own real technical outcomes from your first week and help define how we integrate as we scale.
